newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police suspect passenger in plane blast.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police suspect passenger in plane blast.

text.p: Brazilian police probing a jetliner explosion that killed one person suspect that a suicidal passenger may have planted a bomb, newspapers reported on Saturday.

The Jornal do Brasil daily said the Federal Police, Brazil's equivalent of the U.S. FBI, were increasingly convinced mathematics teacher Leonardo Teodoro de Castro, 59, was to blame for the explosion.

Castro, who survived the July 9 explosion on a TAM Fokker-100 airliner with slight injuries, has been in a Sao Paulo hospital since last weekend after being run over by a bus in what police believe was also a suicide attempt.
"Documents seized in his home reveal, according to the police, a depressive man who has been accused of one attempted murder and at least two suicide attempts," Jornal do Brasil said.
No one was available at Federal Police headquarters to confirm the report.

A 38-year-old engineer was sucked out of the TAM plane when the explosion blew a six-foot by four-foot (two metres by 1.3-metre) hole in the fuselage. The victim plunged 7,200 feet (2,400 metres) to his death.
Newspapers said Castro gave confusing testimony to police after the midair explosion, lying about where he had been staying and why he was on the plane.
They said their suspicions were deepened when witnesses claimed the professor had thrown himself in front of the bus three days after the blast on the TAM flight.

Globo television said lawyers for Castro's family had criticised police for treating passengers aggressively after the explosion. The lawyers said Castro had given confusing testimony because he was in shock.
Brazilian authorities have since boosted security in the country's airports, installing metal detectors and X-ray equipment capable of detecting explosive substances.
